newsitem.title: USA: PairGain falls on pricing, rival technology fears.
newsitem.headline: PairGain falls on pricing, rival technology fears.

text.p: The stock of Pairgain Technologies Inc., a top supplier of high-speed corporate data access equipment, slumped for the second consecutive session running Monday amid fears that even faster Internet access technologies will threaten its market-leading position.
Several Wall Street analysts also repeated recent concerns about downward pricing pressure on PairGain products, even as many of the same analysts continued to recommend the stock.

PairGain fell on Monday to $15.75, down $1.50, a new year-low for the often volatile issue. The stock was the most actively traded Nasdaq stock with volume of 18.6 million shares. It was also the most active Nasdaq issue Friday when it fell $3.875 to $17.25.

Tustin, Calif.-based Pairgain holds an estimated 70 percent of the market for equipment known as High bit-rate Digital Subscriber Line, or HDSL, a low-cost replacement for high-speed phone lines used by corporations to transmit data.
PairGain officials had acknowledged seeing rising price pressures on its equipment at an investor conference three weeks ago, analysts said.
These concerns were stoked anew last Thursday when another HDSL supplier, Teltrend Inc., warned of flat revenue growth for its fourth fiscal quarter ending in July.
PairGain stock has lost more than 60 percent of its value since mid-February, when it traded above $40.
Adding fuel to the sell-off are warnings from industry analysts that the HDSL market is maturing and growth is slowing.
The action is seen as shifting to an emerging data transmission method known as Asymetrical Digital Subscriber Line (ADSL), with data rates up to 10 times faster than HDSL.
ADSL is targeted at residential consumers, not corporate users, and remains significantly more expensive than HDSL.

But ADSL's exponentially higher speed, its potential to replace HDSL among corporate computer users and the prospect of widescale regional deployment by phone carriers has put pressure on PairGain to develop its own ADSL alternative.
